content:
The test image shows split stems/roots on soil. Key features:
- External stem tissue is bleached/whitish-tan
- Internal stem cavity contains large, black masses/sclerotia
- Stems appear dried and hollowed

This strongly suggests White Mold (black sclerotia inside bleached stems) or Charcoal Rot (tiny microsclerotia). The large black internal structures look more like White Mold sclerotia. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows White Mold's characteristic black sclerotia and bleached stems. The test image matches perfectly: split stems with bleached/white external surface and large black sclerotia masses inside the stem cavity. This is the classic presentation described as "hard, black sclerotia resembling rodent droppings on or inside stems" with "bleached white" stem tissue.
